name: Reaper Farm rfUSDC vault redeem without owner authorisation

classification.summary: ReaperVaultV2 exposes the three-argument ERC-4626 exit path redeem(shares, receiver, owner) (and the matching withdraw) but never checks that msg.sender is owner or holds an allowance from owner, so any caller could burn an arbitrary holder’s vault shares and have the underlying asset paid to an address of their choosing. The attacker contract called redeem with each depositor as owner and its own address as receiver; the three owners drained in the anchor transaction had an allowance of exactly 0 to the attacker contract at block 44045360.

loss.notes: Scoped to the rfUSDC vault 0xcda5dea176f2df95082f4dadb96255bdb2bc7c7d, the only Reaper vault that executes in the anchor transaction. Its Withdraw(caller,receiver,owner,assets,shares) log stream from creation to block 44060000 contains 13 events with caller != owner attributable to the attacker, spread over three transactions at blocks 44045361, 44045487 and 44045900, and their assets sum to exactly 596,685.496653 USDC; the attacker receiver 0x2c177d20b1b1d68cc85d3215904a7bb6629ca954 bridged out that exact amount (596685496653 units) at block 44046708 in transaction 0x73a62117b6b88dc6e8384dce596392f995f1f37a10f6dc05f4bbf881e4be6bc5. The 14 later third-party redeems on the same vault (blocks 44052039-44053339, caller 0x1e71aee6081f62053123140aacc7a06021d77348, receiver the safe 0x539ef36c804e4d735d8cab69e8e441c12d4b88e0, about 25,600 USDC) are a rescue sweep of the remaining balances and are excluded; that receiver has made no outbound transfer. The same campaign also drained the sibling vaults rfETH 0x58c60b6df933ff5615890ddddcdd280bad53f1c1, rfWFTM 0xa6313302b3ceff2727f19aaa30d7240d5b3cd9cd, rfBTC 0xeb7761d05a31769d35073f703dd3a41f3ca9bd3d, rfDAI 0x77dc33dc0278d21398cb9b16cbff99c1b712a87a and rfUSDT 0xa9a9db466685f977f9ecee347958bcef90498177, which brings the widely reported campaign total to about USD 1.7M; those vaults are separate deployments with distinct runtime code hashes, none of them executes in this anchor transaction, and their value is not counted here.

lastCodeChange.description: The vault is a plain non-upgradeable deployment: eth_getCode is empty at blocks 41839238 and 41839239 and 16,821 bytes from block 41839240, and keccak(eth_getCode) is 0xd056c916021b116be7449251fe457147d6fcdc124a4a4fa604e271054ad0f085 at the creation block and unchanged at blocks 41900000, 42500000, 43000000, 43500000, 44000000 and 44045360, which is also the code hash the prestateTracer reports inside the anchor transaction. The EIP-1967 implementation, beacon and admin slots and the legacy OpenZeppelin implementation slot all read zero at block 44045360, and the anchor trace contains no DELEGATECALL out of the vault, so no proxy or module indirection supplies its code.

sources.note: Re-anchored. The v1 snapshot anchored to 0xc929f3b9312ff26be0adb1c3ff832dbdafdcbcaad33d002744effd515e53c9d5, which is the third and last attacker transaction against this vault. Reading every Withdraw(address,address,address,uint256,uint256) log (topic 0xfbde797d201c681b91056529119e0b02407c7bb96a4a2c75c01fc9667232c8db) the vault emitted between its creation block 41839240 and block 44060000 gives 76 events, of which 27 have caller != owner and none before block 44045361; the first is log 144 of 0x9f40542ed53737b6aa0c17a2ab0c1f295b665ed83f9f8e3c66e9161a64d684cc at block 44045361 index 4, which is the new anchor. Root cause is confirmed onchain rather than only from the PoC: the three owners redeemed in the anchor transaction had allowance(owner, 0x8162a5e187128565ace634e76fdd083cb04d0145) == 0 at block 44045360, and the exploit contract itself only received code at block 44045179, four minutes earlier. The vault is a direct non-upgradeable contract, not a proxy: EIP-1967 implementation/beacon/admin slots and the legacy OpenZeppelin implementation slot all read zero at block 44045360, the anchor trace has no DELEGATECALL out of the vault, and keccak(eth_getCode) equals 0xd056c916021b116be7449251fe457147d6fcdc124a4a4fa604e271054ad0f085 at the creation block, at five sampled intermediate blocks, at block 44045360 and in the anchor prestate, while eth_getCode is empty at blocks 41839238 and 41839239, so the only executable-code change is the deployment and the code is 2,650,334 s (30d 16h 12m 14s) old. Creation is the top-level contract-creation transaction 0x1fef1cb729b5a6263de7b190b560130ff62ff86bc6bde3189b631c3b4856d514, index 1 of block 41839240, sender 0x6539519e69343535a2af6583d9bae3ad74c6a293, which is not an attacker address. Scope: Reaper’s campaign hit six vaults, but only rfUSDC 0xcda5dea176f2df95082f4dadb96255bdb2bc7c7d executes in this anchor, the six vaults are separate deployments with different runtime code hashes, so the other five are neither targets nor loss of this record; the loss here is the 596,685.496653 USDC the attacker took out of rfUSDC across three transactions, cross-checked against the exact amount its receiver bridged out at block 44046708. Fantom note: fantom.drpc.org serves archive eth_getCode and eth_getStorageAt but frequently answers eth_getTransactionByHash and debug_traceTransaction from a pruned node; the traces and prestate here were taken from fantom.api.onfinality.io and the full-range eth_getLogs from rpcapi.fantom.network.
